Aisha, after Khaula offers herself and the verse on postponing wives' turns comes, says the Prophet's Lord hastens to please him; Ibn Abbas says the Prophet married in Ihram.
Ali reports the Prophet forbade temporary marriage at Khaibar; Ibn Abbas allowed it in need, it was allowed in an army for three nights, and Ali said it was cancelled.
Women offer themselves to the Prophet in marriage, one praised by Anas; Umar offers Hafsa to Uthman and Abu Bakr; Durra is unlawful to the Prophet as a foster niece.
One may hint, not openly declare, a proposal to a widow in her waiting period; the Prophet saw Aisha in a dream and looked closely at a woman offering herself.
Aisha says the Prophet ended pre-Islamic marriages except asking a guardian for a woman's hand; guardians may not stop orphan girls or a divorced sister marrying, and Umar offers Hafsa.
Aisha says the Prophet married her when she was six and consummated the marriage when she was nine, and she stayed with him nine years.
A matron must be consulted, a virgin's silence is consent; Khansa's marriage against her wish is annulled; the Prophet marries a woman to a man for the Quran he knows.
No man should propose to a woman engaged to his brother or undercut another's bargain, and suspicion and spying are forbidden; Abu Bakr kept secret the Prophet's mention of Hafsa.
After two men from the east give speeches, the Prophet says some eloquent speech has the influence of magic.
After Ar-Rubayyi's wedding the Prophet sits with her while girls beat tambourines mourning her father, killed at Badr, and he stops a line claiming he knows tomorrow.
Abdur-Rahman gives a date-stone's weight of gold as bridal gift, a man is wed for the Quran he knows, and the Prophet says marry even with an iron ring.
The conditions most binding are those of the marriage contract, and a woman may not demand that her would-be husband divorce another wife.
The Prophet blesses Abdur-Rahman and tells him to give a banquet, even of one sheep; he gives one for Zainab, and Ansar women bless Aisha as a bride.
A prophet bars grooms yet to consummate from his campaign; the Prophet consummates with Aisha and Safiyya, tells Jabir he will have Anmat, and notes the Ansar like wedding amusement.
At the Prophet's wedding to Zainab, Um Sulaim's dish feeds batches of guests, and after some linger he recites the verse telling guests to disperse after eating.
When a necklace Aisha borrowed was lost and searchers prayed without ablution, the verse of Tayammum was revealed, and Usaid bin Hudair praises the blessing she brought.
Saying Allah's name and asking protection from Satan when having intercourse with one's wife keeps Satan from harming any child destined from it.
After guests lingered at Zainab's wedding banquet the Hijab verses came; the Prophet's best banquet was one sheep for Zainab, others were of hais or barley.
Wedding invitations must be accepted, Ibn Umar going even when fasting; the worst feast invites only the rich; the Prophet would accept a trotter; Abu Usaid's bride served the guests.
Seeing women and children returning from a wedding, the Prophet rises and tells the Ansar they are the most beloved of all people to him.
The Prophet will not enter where Aisha placed a cushion with pictures, saying picture-makers will be punished and angels do not enter a house with pictures.
At Abu Usaid's wedding his bride alone prepared and served the food and gave the Prophet a drink of dates soaked overnight.
Woman is like a rib that breaks if straightened, so the Prophet urges care for women; Ibn Umar says men spoke freely with their wives only after the Prophet's death.
Everyone is a guardian responsible for his wards: the ruler for his people, a man for his family, a wife for her husband's house, a slave for his master's property.
Eleven women describe their husbands and the Prophet tells Aisha he is to her as Abu Zar to Um Zar; he screens her as she watches Ethiopians play.
Umar names Aisha and Hafsa as the two wives in verse 66:4 and tells of the Prophet's twenty-nine days away from his wives, his bare room, and the option verses.
A wife should not fast voluntarily without her husband's leave when he is home, nor admit anyone without his leave, and angels curse a wife refusing his bed until morning.
The Prophet saw that most in Paradise were the poor and most in the Fire were women, explaining after the eclipse prayer that they were ungrateful to their husbands.
Abdullah bin Amr is told his wife has a right over him, and everyone is a guardian: a man of his family, a wife of her husband's house and children.
The Prophet swore to stay away from his wives for a month, sat in his upper room, and returned after twenty-nine days, saying the month can be twenty-nine days.
Do not flog a wife like a slave then lie with her; Allah curses women lengthening hair artificially, even at a husband's wish; a wife facing divorce may waive rights.
Companions practised coitus interruptus while the Quran was being revealed, including with female captives, and the Prophet says every soul destined to exist will come into existence.
The Prophet drew lots among his wives for journeys, kept turns and died in Aisha's house; a virgin bride gets seven days, a matron three; Umar cautioned Hafsa about Aisha.
A woman asked if she may claim her husband gave her what he had not, to tease his other wife; the Prophet likened this to wearing two garments of falsehood.
None has a greater sense of ghira than Allah, so He forbade illegal sexual intercourse; it is provoked when a believer does what He prohibited, and none loves praise more.
Ghira and jealousy: Zubair's, Umar's, a wife's who broke a co-wife's dish, Aisha's over Khadija; the Prophet refused Ali another wife, since what hurts Fatima hurts him.
Among the portents of the Hour: religious knowledge taken away, ignorance, illegal sexual intercourse and drinking widespread, and women so outnumbering men that one man looks after fifty.
Men must not enter upon women or be alone with one without a mahram, in-laws above all; the Prophet spoke aside with an Ansari woman and barred an effeminate man.
Aisha watched Ethiopians play, screened by the Prophet; women may go out for needs or to the mosque; foster uncles may enter; wives must not describe women to husbands.
Solomon meant to go round a hundred wives to beget fighters in Allah's cause but forgot to say 'If Allah will', and only one bore a child, half a person.
